post_doing: Lists the 8 ways Josh works out what software a company runs, ranked from the two everyone in go-to-market uses down to the ones hardly anyone uses, with the effort each takes. Structure (rows along a single direction arrow) taken from a Fletch visual Josh shared; built in the Slingshot GTM brand with his wordmark at his request.

Lists the 8 ways Josh works out what software a company runs, ordered from easiest to hardest to use, shaded from pale to deep green by effort. Version 2 after Josh's feedback: his order (password reset, then login portals, then DNS and banners as hardest), more colour, no mono labels, green highlight on the title. Structure taken from a Fletch visual he shared; his brand and wordmark at his request.

Version 3, the one Josh chose. Lists the 8 ways Josh works out what software a company runs. The arrow runs from 'Everyone uses' to 'Hardly anyone uses' (the hook's angle); rows are shaded in his navy ramp by effort, with the effort rating beside each. Title with 'software a company runs' in his green italic, portrait 4:5 to match his 19 October visual, wordmark at his request. Structure taken from a Fletch visual he shared.

Version 4, the final image Josh chose to post with this. Titled "Tech stack detection methods" (his wording, so it no longer repeats the post's opening line). The 8 methods run down an arrow from 'Everyone uses' to 'Hardly anyone uses', shaded in his navy ramp by effort, with the effort rating beside each. Portrait 4:5, wordmark at his request. Structure taken from a Fletch visual he shared.
Rasteriser proof for the 26 October fix. Not for publication.
